subproblem.title: Regular-point balls of a C¹ map have embedded C¹ submanifold images
subproblem.statement: For all n, p ∈ ℕ (ℝᵈ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)), every map G : ℝⁿ → ℝᵖ of class C¹ (ContDiff ℝ 1 G), and every x ∈ ℝⁿ at which the Fréchet derivative DG(x) = fderiv ℝ G x is injective, there is σ > 0 such that G(B_σ(x)) (B_σ(x) = Metric.ball x σ) is an n-dimensional embedded C¹ submanifold of ℝᵖ in the sense of IsC1Submanifold n. That is, for every y ∈ G(B_σ(x)) there are an open V ⊆ ℝⁿ, an open W ⊆ ℝᵖ with y ∈ W, and a map ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝᵖ such that: ψ is C¹ and injective on V; ψ(V) = W ∩ G(B_σ(x)); V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W; and fderiv ℝ ψ z is injective for every z ∈ V.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n p : ℕ) (G : Rn n → Rn p), ContDiff ℝ 1 G → ∀ x : Rn n, Function.Injective (fderiv ℝ G x) → ∃ σ : ℝ, 0 < σ ∧ IsC1Submanifold n (G '' Metric.ball x σ)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Simon, Ch. 3, proof of Lemma 1.2, chapter-03.txt lines 61-64 (printed p. 70): "if the Jacobian [of] G_ij is non-zero at a point x, then there is a σ > 0 such that G_ij(B_σ(x)) is an n-dimensional C¹ submanifold of ℝⁿ (with G_ij providing a local representation in a neighborhood of the point y = G_ij(x))".
Two of the parent's errata apply:
- (iv) "of ℝⁿ" should read "of ℝ^{n+ℓ}"; here the target is an arbitrary ℝᵖ.
- (v) σ must be chosen so that G is injective on a closed ball B̄_{2σ}(x). This gives the properness required by the definition of an embedded C¹ submanifold, Ch. 2 (4.1) (chapter-02.txt lines 849-860), transcribed as IsC1Submanifold.
This is Step 7 of the parent proof (node root.submanifold_cover-a1), with the relatively open set W given explicitly.

Notation: ℝᵈ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d); |·| is the Euclidean norm and ‖·‖ the operator norm; B_r(x) = Metric.ball x r and B̄_r(x) = Metric.closedBall x r; DG(z) = fderiv ℝ G z.

Hypotheses: n, p ∈ ℕ; G : ℝⁿ → ℝᵖ with ContDiff ℝ 1 G; x ∈ ℝⁿ with DG(x) injective.
Goal: some σ > 0 with IsC1Submanifold n (G(B_σ(x))).

1. Regularity of G. G is C¹ and 1 ≠ 0. So G is differentiable at every point with derivative DG(z), G is continuous, and z ↦ DG(z) is continuous from ℝⁿ to L(ℝⁿ, ℝᵖ) with the operator norm (Mathlib ContDiff.differentiable, ContDiff.continuous, ContDiff.continuous_fderiv).

2. Lower bound for L := DG(x). L is an injective linear map on the finite-dimensional space ℝⁿ, so there is c > 0 with |Lv| ≥ c|v| for all v ∈ ℝⁿ.
Proof: LinearMap.injective_iff_antilipschitz gives K > 0 with |v − w| ≤ K|Lv − Lw| for all v, w. Take w = 0 and c := 1/K.
For n ≥ 1 one may equivalently take c := min_{|v|=1} |Lv|, which is positive by compactness of the unit sphere and injectivity. For n = 0 every c > 0 works, because v = 0.

3. Choice of σ. DG is continuous at x, so there is δ > 0 with ‖DG(z) − L‖ < c/2 whenever |z − x| < δ.
Put σ := δ/4 > 0 and B̄ := B̄_{2σ}(x) = B̄_{δ/2}(x).
Every z ∈ B̄ has |z − x| ≤ δ/2 < δ, so ‖DG(z) − L‖ ≤ c/2 for all z ∈ B̄.

4. G is quantitatively injective on B̄.
Let h(w) := G(w) − Lw. Then h is differentiable with Dh(w) = DG(w) − L, so ‖Dh(w)‖ ≤ c/2 on B̄.
B̄ is convex, so the mean value inequality (Mathlib Convex.norm_image_sub_le_of_norm_hasFDerivWithin_le) gives, for all z, z' ∈ B̄:
|h(z) − h(z')| ≤ (c/2)|z − z'|, that is, |G(z) − G(z') − L(z − z')| ≤ (c/2)|z − z'|.
By the triangle inequality and Step 2:
|G(z) − G(z')| ≥ |L(z − z')| − |G(z) − G(z') − L(z − z')| ≥ c|z − z'| − (c/2)|z − z'| = (c/2)|z − z'|.
So if G(z) = G(z') with z, z' ∈ B̄, then (c/2)|z − z'| ≤ 0, hence z = z'. Thus G is injective on B̄.

5. DG(z) is injective for every z ∈ B̄.
For v ∈ ℝⁿ: |DG(z)v| ≥ |Lv| − |(DG(z) − L)v| ≥ c|v| − (c/2)|v| = (c/2)|v|.
If DG(z)v = DG(z)w, then DG(z)(v − w) = 0 by linearity. So (c/2)|v − w| ≤ 0 and v = w.

6. The chart data. Let V := B_σ(x), S := G(V), A := B̄ ∖ B_σ(x) and W := ℝᵖ ∖ G(A).
- Since σ < 2σ, V ⊆ B̄_σ(x) ⊆ B̄.
- A is closed (a closed ball minus an open ball) and bounded, hence compact.
- G(A) is compact as a continuous image, hence closed in ℝᵖ. Therefore W is open. V is open.
W is the open set of the parent proof with W ∩ G(B̄) = S: if y = G(z) with z ∈ B̄ and y ∉ G(A), then z ∉ A, so z ∈ B_σ(x). The converse inclusion is Step 7.

7. S ⊆ W, hence W ∩ S = S.
Let z ∈ V and suppose G(z) ∈ G(A), say G(z) = G(a) with a ∈ A. Both z and a lie in B̄, so Step 4 gives z = a ∈ A = B̄ ∖ B_σ(x). This contradicts z ∈ B_σ(x).
So G(z) ∈ W for every z ∈ V, i.e. S ⊆ W and W ∩ S = S.

8. Properness. Let K ⊆ W be compact. Claim: V ∩ G⁻¹(K) = B̄_σ(x) ∩ G⁻¹(K).
- ⊆ holds because B_σ(x) ⊆ B̄_σ(x).
- ⊇: let z ∈ B̄_σ(x) with G(z) ∈ K. If z ∉ B_σ(x), then z ∈ B̄_σ(x) ∖ B_σ(x) ⊆ B̄ ∖ B_σ(x) = A. Then G(z) ∈ G(A) = ℝᵖ ∖ W, contradicting G(z) ∈ K ⊆ W. Hence z ∈ V.
This is the parent's sequential argument: a limit z* ∈ B̄_σ(x) of points z_k ∈ V with G(z_k) ∈ K has G(z*) ∈ K, and therefore lies in V.
Now B̄_σ(x) is compact (closed and bounded in ℝⁿ). K is closed (compact in the Hausdorff space ℝᵖ) and G is continuous, so G⁻¹(K) is closed. Hence B̄_σ(x) ∩ G⁻¹(K) is a closed subset of a compact set, so it is compact, and V ∩ G⁻¹(K) is compact.

9. Verification of IsC1Submanifold n S. Let y ∈ S. Take V and W as in Step 6 and ψ := G. Then:
- V is open and W is open (Step 6);
- y ∈ S ⊆ W (Step 7);
- ψ is C¹ on V, because G is C¹ on ℝⁿ (ContDiff.contDiffOn);
- ψ is injective on V, because V ⊆ B̄ (Step 4);
- ψ(V) = S = W ∩ S (Step 7);
- V ∩ ψ⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ W (Step 8);
- fderiv ℝ ψ z = DG(z) is injective for every z ∈ V ⊆ B̄ (Step 5).
These are exactly the eight conditions of IsC1Submanifold n S at y.

10. Conclusion. σ = δ/4 > 0 and G(B_σ(x)) satisfies IsC1Submanifold n. For n = 0 the argument is unchanged: ℝ⁰ is a point, B_σ(x) = B̄_σ(x) = B̄ = {x}, A = ∅ and W = ℝᵖ. ∎
proof_key_steps: Since DG(x) is injective on the finite-dimensional ℝⁿ, there is c > 0 with |DG(x)v| ≥ c|v| (antilipschitz constant; any c works for n = 0).
Continuity of DG gives σ := δ/4 > 0 with ‖DG(z) − DG(x)‖ ≤ c/2 on B̄ := B̄_{2σ}(x).
Mean value inequality for G − DG(x) on the convex B̄ gives |G(z) − G(z')| ≥ (c/2)|z − z'|, so G is injective on B̄; also |DG(z)v| ≥ (c/2)|v|, so DG(z) is injective on B̄.
W := ℝᵖ ∖ G(B̄ ∖ B_σ(x)) is open (compact image) and contains G(B_σ(x)) by injectivity on B̄.
Properness: for compact K ⊆ W, B_σ(x) ∩ G⁻¹(K) = B̄_σ(x) ∩ G⁻¹(K), which is compact. The single chart (B_σ(x), W, G) verifies IsC1Submanifold n at every point.

Step 9 verifies every frozen chart condition. The argument includes n = 0 and requires no missing dimension hypothesis. It is complete, non-circular and directly formalizable. subproblem.title: C¹ images are covered by an Hⁿ-null set and countably many embedded C¹ n-submanifolds
subproblem.statement: For all n, p ∈ ℕ (ℝᵈ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d)) and every map G : ℝⁿ → ℝᵖ of class C¹ (ContDiff ℝ 1 G), there are a set N₀ ⊆ ℝᵖ with Hⁿ(N₀) = 0 (Hⁿ = μHE[n], applied as an outer measure) and sets N_k ⊆ ℝᵖ (k ∈ ℕ), each an n-dimensional embedded C¹ submanifold in the sense of IsC1Submanifold n, such that the range G(ℝⁿ) ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃_k N_k.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n p : ℕ) (G : Rn n → Rn p), ContDiff ℝ 1 G → ∃ (N₀ : Set (Rn p)) (N : ℕ → Set (Rn p)), μHE[n] N₀ = 0 ∧ (∀ k, IsC1Submanifold n (N k)) ∧ Set.range G ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃ k, N k
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Simon, Ch. 3, proof of Lemma 1.2, chapter-03.txt lines 61-65 (printed p. 70), applied to a single C¹ map G : ℝⁿ → ℝᵖ:
"Now by the area formula Lⁿ({x : J_{G_ij} = 0} [parent erratum (iii): Hⁿ(G_ij({x : J_{G_ij}(x) = 0})) = 0] whereas if the Jacobian G_ij is non-zero at a point x, then there is a σ > 0 such that G_ij(B_σ(x)) is an n-dimensional C¹ submanifold ... So ∪_{ij} G_ij can be written as the union of a set of measure zero and countably many n-dimensional C¹ submanifolds of ℝ^{n+ℓ}".
This is Steps 6 and 8 of the parent proof (node root.submanifold_cover-a1). Step 7 is the sibling regular_ball_submanifold (Lean: c1_regular_point_ball_image_isC1Submanifold).

Notation: ℝᵈ = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin d); B_r(x) = Metric.ball x r; DG(z) = fderiv ℝ G z; Hⁿ = μHE[n]; Lⁿ = volume, which equals μHE[n] on ℝⁿ (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume).

Hypotheses: n, p ∈ ℕ; G : ℝⁿ → ℝᵖ with ContDiff ℝ 1 G.
Goal: N₀ ⊆ ℝᵖ and (N_k)_{k∈ℕ} with Hⁿ(N₀) = 0, IsC1Submanifold n (N_k) for every k, and range G ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃_k N_k.

1. Critical and regular sets. G is C¹, so it is differentiable at every point with derivative DG(z) (ContDiff.differentiable).
Let Crit(G) := {z ∈ ℝⁿ : DG(z) is not injective} and Reg(G) := ℝⁿ ∖ Crit(G).
With JG(z) := normDet(DG(z)) = √det(DG(z)* DG(z)), we have Crit(G) = {JG = 0} (Mathlib LinearMap.normDet_eq_zero_tfae; SimonGMT Chapter02.areaJacobianAt_eq_zero_iff_not_injective).
Since G is differentiable everywhere, Crit(G) = {z : G is differentiable at z and DG(z) is not injective}.

2. The critical image is Hⁿ-null (parent Step 6). Put N₀ := G(Crit(G)).
For k ∈ ℕ let s_k := B_k(0), an open, convex, bounded set.
- DG is continuous, hence bounded by some C_k on the compact B̄_k(0). By the mean value inequality, G is C_k-Lipschitz on the convex set s_k.
- Crit(G) = {JG = 0} is closed, since JG is the continuous normDet composed with the continuous z ↦ DG(z). So the weight w := 1_{Crit(G)} is Borel.
Apply the weighted area formula for Lipschitz maps on Lebesgue-measurable domains (Simon Ch. 2 (3.5); SimonGMT Chapter02.weighted_area_formula_lipschitzOn_fiberSum with s := s_k, f := G, and this w):
∫ Σ_{z ∈ s_k ∩ G⁻¹(y)} 1_{Crit(G)}(z) dHⁿ(y) = ∫_{s_k} J_G^{s_k}(z) 1_{Crit(G)}(z) dLⁿ(z).
Here J_G^{s_k}(z) = normDet(fderivWithin ℝ G s_k z) = JG(z) for z in the open set s_k.
- The right side is 0, because JG = 0 on Crit(G).
- The left integrand is Hⁿ-a.e. measurable (SimonGMT aemeasurable_weightedAreaFiberSum_lipschitzOn), so it vanishes for Hⁿ-a.e. y.
- For y ∈ G(Crit(G) ∩ s_k) the fiber sum is ≥ 1: it contains a term z ∈ Crit(G) ∩ s_k with G(z) = y, of weight 1.
Hence Hⁿ(G(Crit(G) ∩ s_k)) = 0 for every k. Since ℝⁿ = ⋃_k s_k, countable subadditivity gives
Hⁿ(N₀) = Hⁿ(⋃_k G(Crit(G) ∩ s_k)) = 0.
Library form of this step: SimonGMT Chapter02.area_image_criticalSet_eq_zero G states
μHE[finrank ℝ ℝⁿ](G({z : DifferentiableAt ℝ G z ∧ ¬ Injective (DG(z))})) = 0.
By Step 1 that set is Crit(G), and finrank ℝ ℝⁿ = n by finrank_euclideanSpace_fin.

3. Regular balls (parent Step 7). For each x ∈ Reg(G), apply the sibling regular_ball_submanifold to G (which is C¹) and x (where DG(x) is injective). It gives σ_x > 0 such that G(B_{σ_x}(x)) satisfies IsC1Submanifold n.
For x ∈ Crit(G) set σ_x := 1; these balls are never used.

4. Lindelöf (parent Step 8). ℝⁿ is second countable, and {B_{σ_x}(x) : x ∈ Reg(G)} is a family of open sets indexed by Reg(G).
By Mathlib TopologicalSpace.isOpen_biUnion_countable there is a countable T ⊆ Reg(G) with
⋃_{x∈T} B_{σ_x}(x) = ⋃_{x∈Reg(G)} B_{σ_x}(x).
Every x ∈ Reg(G) lies in its own ball (σ_x > 0), so Reg(G) ⊆ ⋃_{x∈T} B_{σ_x}(x). Openness of Reg(G), noted in the parent, is not needed here.

5. Enumeration, padded with ∅ (parent Step 9).
The family 𝒟 := {∅} ∪ {G(B_{σ_x}(x)) : x ∈ T} of subsets of ℝᵖ is countable (the image of the countable T plus one set) and nonempty. So there is a sequence (N_k)_{k∈ℕ} with {N_k : k ∈ ℕ} = 𝒟 (Mathlib Set.Countable.exists_eq_range).
Each N_k is one of:
- ∅, which satisfies IsC1Submanifold n vacuously (the condition quantifies over y ∈ ∅);
- G(B_{σ_x}(x)) for some x ∈ T ⊆ Reg(G), which satisfies IsC1Submanifold n by Step 3.

6. Covering. Let y ∈ range G, say y = G(z).
- If z ∈ Crit(G), then y ∈ G(Crit(G)) = N₀.
- Otherwise z ∈ Reg(G), so by Step 4 z ∈ B_{σ_x}(x) for some x ∈ T. Then y ∈ G(B_{σ_x}(x)) ∈ 𝒟, i.e. y ∈ N_k for some k.
Hence range G ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃_k N_k.

7. Conclusion. N₀ and (N_k) satisfy Hⁿ(N₀) = 0 (Step 2), IsC1Submanifold n (N_k) for all k (Step 5), and range G ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃_k N_k (Step 6). ∎
proof_key_steps: G is differentiable everywhere. Crit(G) = {DG not injective} = {JG = 0}, and Reg(G) is its complement.
Hⁿ(G(Crit(G))) = 0 by the weighted area formula on the balls B_k(0) with weight 1_{Crit(G)} (library form: SimonGMT area_image_criticalSet_eq_zero, with finrank ℝ ℝⁿ = n). Set N₀ := G(Crit(G)).
For each x ∈ Reg(G), the sibling regular_ball_submanifold gives σ_x > 0 with G(B_{σ_x}(x)) an IsC1Submanifold n.
Lindelöf (isOpen_biUnion_countable) gives a countable T ⊆ Reg(G) with Reg(G) ⊆ ⋃_{x∈T} B_{σ_x}(x).
Enumerate {∅} ∪ {G(B_{σ_x}(x)) : x ∈ T} by ℕ (∅ is vacuously a submanifold). Then range G ⊆ N₀ ∪ ⋃_k N_k.

The weighted-area explanation correctly handles local Lipschitz bounds, measurable weights and almost-everywhere vanishing of multiplicity. The proof then uses regular_ball_submanifold, extracts a countable family by Lindelöf, adds ∅ to permit enumeration even for an empty family, and proves the range inclusion pointwise. Its sole child dependency is correctly directed and acyclic. The proof is complete and does not invoke the parent. The bare lean_name is unreserved and its type elaborates independently. Combined with the registered approximation dependency, null-image estimates and the library reverse implication, these children prove the exact selected parent.
